summary: After an unprecedented storm hit Eastville on October 15, 2023, causing blackouts and communication outages, officials held an After-Action Review (AAR) on November 10, 2023 to evaluate the emergency response. The review gathered input from responders, utilities, volunteers, and residents, and found problems with inter-agency coordination, communication channels, and aging infrastructure. Resulting actions include system upgrades, simulation training, grid and cyber investment, psychological first aid, public education, and scheduled follow-ups.
one_line: Eastville's After-Action Review of the October 2023 storm outage identified coordination and infrastructure gaps and launched improvements in training, technology, and community engagement.
key_facts: On October 15, 2023, Eastville was hit by an unprecedented storm that caused massive blackouts and severed digital communication for days.
The After-Action Review (AAR) was conducted on November 10, 2023 and facilitated by independent consultant Dr. Emily Larson.
Harry Thompson, Director of Eastville's Office of Emergency Management, described the AAR as 'a structured evaluation' of what occurred, what was supposed to happen, and where to improve.
The AAR involved emergency responders, utility companies, volunteer organizations, and representatives from affected neighborhoods.
Larson said data is gathered through interviews, surveys, and operational logs to build a comprehensive picture of the incident and response.
Local residents were invited to submit experiences and suggestions through online platforms; community leader Michael Rodriguez of South Eastville said reviews usually 'happen behind closed doors'.

Inter-agency coordination was initially stymied by jurisdictional issues, and Samantha Brooks of the state emergency response team said communication channels were not as streamlined as assumed, slowing logistical decisions.
Old infrastructure struggled under the strain, and the scale of outages overwhelmed repair crews and led to longer restoration times.
Larry Foster, head of Eastville Utilities, said the utility is upgrading systems and training emergency liaison officers to work with other agencies.
Chief Maria Vasquez of Eastville's Emergency Service Department said simulation exercises are now routine and based on AAR lessons, with increasingly complex scenarios.
Eastville has allocated funds for grid modernization and for enhancing cyber resiliency against digital disruptions.
Dr. Jasmine Patel, a mental health consultant, highlighted psychological support, with systems being set up for psychological first aid for responders and residents.
Public education campaigns were identified as a preparedness gap and are now a priority, according to Thompson.
Follow-ups are scheduled to evaluate progress on implementing action plan recommendations.
